conflicts.description: The manual prints opposite settings for option switch 8. The `NINE BALL SWITCH ASSIGNMENTS` page (PDF page 11) gives `8 Background Sound` ON = On and OFF = Off; the adjustment table on PDF page 13 gives `BACKGROUND SOUND` `SOUND OFF` = ON and `SOUND ON` = OFF. Both are this game's own manual and nothing else retained names the setting: the known-working scripts' option menu labels this bit with another game's text (`Missile wows light on equal value`), and PinMAME boots with every option switch OFF. A recreation that exposes the option therefore cannot tell which setting gives background sound. Resolution path: boot nineball with option switch 8 ON and OFF and compare the sound board commands over an idle stretch of play; tools/run_pinmame_harness.py has no option-switch input yet, so the probe needs one added, or an owner can flip S8 on a machine.

mechanisms.behavior: Three trough switches under the apron, printed 37, 36 and 33 from left to right on the location drawing; the ball at the right end rests on the outhole switch (public 33) in front of the outhole kicker (public 7, `Outhole Kicker` J-26-1200), and the other two wait on 36 and 37. The known-working scripts start with all three balls in the trough. Pressing the credit button resets the drop targets and the outhole kicker moves the ball to the shooter lane (manual); in the retained runs the ROM fires the eight-bank reset (17), both three-bank resets (3, 4) and the outhole kicker (7) together and repeats them about every 1.2 s while 33 stays closed. After a drain the bonus times the multiplier is collected, the ball and player advance and the next ball is served the same way; an extra ball is played without advancing. Both scripts model the trough as a virtual ball stack and serve from a shooter-lane kicker.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball outhole trough and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: A kick-out hole (switch 34, coil public 8, `Lane Kicker` J-28-2300) at the foot of the left lane, with the lane's middle (38) and top (39) switches above it, each closed by a ball resting behind the one below. Before object 5 is lit the ROM spots the lit objects with the knock-down coils, waiting for each target's switch before it fires the next, then ejects the ball and resets the eight-bank (retained kick-out-spot run). Once object 5 is lit the hole captures the ball: the ROM spots, keeps the ball and serves another from the trough; a ball on 38 behind it is captured the same way, and a third ball on 39 releases all three, the ROM firing public 8 once for each ball as it drops onto 34 (retained lock-lane run; manual: `Making Object No. 9 or capturing all 3 balls will release all captured balls for play`). Capturing on 34 or 38 can award a shoot-again (manual). Home state: empty.
mechanisms.label: Left lane kick-out hole and three-ball lock lane

mechanisms.behavior: Two four-target banks along the left side on one reset coil (`8 Bank Drop Target D-548-9B`; reset public 17, B-24-1600): the upper bank carries objects 2, 4, 6 and 8 from the top (switches 10, 12, 14 and 16) and the lower bank objects 7, 5, 3 and 1 (switches 15, 13, 11 and 9). A target's switch is closed while it is down. Objects 1-7 each have a `Drop Target (Programmable)` knock-down coil (C1-34-3400) that the ROM fires to put the target down: object k's coil is public 16-k (9 for object 7 up to 15 for object 1); object 8 has none. Home state: all eight up. The game is played in order: hitting the lit object scores it, advances the bonus and lights the next; when the lit object is made the ROM resets the bank within about 35 ms and knocks the objects made so far down again, lowest first, each coil fired only after the previous target's switch has closed (retained runs). Lighting object 5 makes the kick-out hole capture; making all eight in order lights the object 9 target and WOW; later rounds light Special and exclude one more low object each time (manual).
mechanisms.label: Left eight-target drop bank (two four-target banks, programmable)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets at the top centre (switches 18, 19, 20 left to right; `3 Bank Drop Target D-580-3J`) on one reset coil (public 4, B-27-2300); no knock-down coils. Home state: all up. With option switch 14 OFF the ROM resets both three-banks only after all six targets are down (retained gameplay run: public 4 and 3 fire on the sixth); with it ON one bank resets at random (manual note 3). The targets score 1,000 or 7,000, completing a bank advances the multiplier, the outside targets award WOW when lit and the targets option switch 17 selects advance the spinner value.
mechanisms.label: Center (top) three-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets on the right (switches 22, 23, 24 top to bottom; `3 Bank Drop Target D-580-3J`) on one reset coil (public 3, B-27-2300); no knock-down coils. Home state: all up. It resets together with the center bank as that record describes, and scores the same way.
mechanisms.label: Right three-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: One drop target below the top-left loop (switch 21; `1 Drop Target C-383-3`) raised by public 20 (Q18, the solenoid table's `LOOP DROP TARGET`). Home state: up. Knocking it down collects and resets the loop value (manual); in the retained gameplay run the ROM pulsed public 20 about 2.6 s after switch 21 closed and again after the target came back up.
mechanisms.label: Single loop drop target

mechanisms.behavior: The loop at the top left is entered under a roll-under gate (`Roll-Under Gate Assembly A-791`) whose switch is public 4; the loop's exit passes the loop drop target. The roll-under and the left lane lower switch (32) score 3,000 and advance the loop value (lamps LOOP 10K to the top value), which the loop target and a lit outlane collect (manual; retained gameplay run). No coil.
mechanisms.label: Top-left loop with roll-under gate

mechanisms.behavior: A spinning target across the right lane (`Spin Target Assembly A-792`); each rotation closes switch 5 once and scores 100 or the highest lit spinner value, and any spin resets the value. The value advances on the three-bank targets option switch 17 selects and goes to the top on the advance-spinner stand-up (35). No coil or home sensor.
mechanisms.label: Right spinning target

mechanisms.behavior: One thumper bumper below the top bank (`Thumper Bumper J-26-1200`). The ROM fires public 5 when switch 31 closes (retained gameplay runs); scores 100 or the highest lit spinner value (manual).
mechanisms.label: Pop (thumper) bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Two J-26-1600 slingshots. The ROM fires each coil when its switch closes: left switch 30 fires public 2 and right switch 29 public 1 (retained gameplay runs). Printed solenoid numbers are 1 (left) and 2 (right). Each scores 10.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: One flipper per side (`Flippers (2)` J-25-475/34-4500), each a dual-winding coil fed from +43 VDC (A2J1-6, fuse F4) through a contact of the flipper enable relay (public 19, printed solenoid 15, CR20 across its coil) to the side's cabinet button. The ROM energizes the relay when a game starts and drops it on a tilt and at game over (retained runs). Each coil's end-of-stroke contact is closed at rest and opens at the end of the stroke to insert the hold winding. PinMAME publishes 46 (right) and 48 (left) with 45 and 47 alongside.
mechanisms.label: Two dual-winding flippers

mechanisms.behavior: A passive bumper at the upper right with a switch (17) and no coil (parts list `Dead Bumper A-578-2`; playfield parts `Rebound Bumper Assembly A-790`; IPDB `Passive bumper (1)`). When lit it spots the lit object: the ROM fired object 1's knock-down coil (public 15) in the retained gameplay run.
mechanisms.label: Top dead bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The playfield parts list names a `Ball Gate Assembly A-611-R` and a `1 Way Gate Assembly A-471` (wire 6A-211), with no coil or switch. They route the ball by its own motion; do not invent a powered diverter.
mechanisms.label: Passive ball gates
